nodes.rationale: Passed 9/9 values cleanly at 2GB triage but 3 subsequently FAILed at 16GB -- direct precedent for why 2GB Tier 1 pass is only a volume filter, not final verdict; also the source of the rejected 5.5-13x warm-up overhead.

nodes.rationale: Staged sizes chosen from k-threshold-characterization (256MB) and o-width-fix triage precedent (2GB); explicitly not sufficient for final verdict since o-width-fix's own 2GB triage later had 3/9 candidates FAIL at 16GB.

nodes.label: Kandidat A (wide-o, no warm-up)
nodes.rationale: Structurally identical to w8_f0_i0 (width=8, empty finalizer); already tested to 16GB in o-width-fix and FAILED (TMFn at K=1, BCFN at K=2/4) -- cited rather than re-run to save VPS compute.

nodes.label: w8_f0_i0 (width=8, empty finalizer, excluded)
nodes.rationale: Excluded from Promotion Tier re-run because structurally identical to Kandidat A, already known FAIL at 16GB; result cited from o-width-fix instead of re-running.

nodes.label: w8_f33_i0 (alt: width=8, ADD(b)->ROT(cons), non-xorshift)
nodes.rationale: Lowest overhead (0.90x) of all 11 winners but structurally unusual: only non-xorshift winner (ADD+ROT), passes despite ADD-alone and ROT-alone both failing individually -- flagged as higher generalization risk outside the 96-K test set.

nodes.label: w8_f9_i0 (recommended: width=8, XORSHIFT(16))
nodes.rationale: First-choice candidate for promotion: second-lowest overhead among 11 winners (1.01x), simplest (1 finalizer instruction, no MUL constant to audit), shift=16 centered in 32-bit word -- easiest to document/justify.

nodes.label: BCFN structural defect (K-small)
nodes.rationale: BCFN defect on small K (FAIL up to K~72, clean from K~96) motivates the entire cycle-operation combo search after init/seed fixes failed.

nodes.label: TMFn defect (Kandidat A, K=1)
nodes.rationale: w8_f0_i0 (finalizer-empty wide-o) fails K=1 with TMFn (not BCFN), R~=+13.6 @16GB, distinct failure mode from BCFN seen at K=2/4.

nodes.label: Tier 0 avalanche gate (min-per-bit)

nodes.label: K-kecil Singleblock Structural Defect
nodes.rationale: Root cause: initial block state (a=cons=key,b=0,c=0,d=0) is identical across keys/blocks; first iteration (i=255) mixes with only 2 fixed M[] slots via 'o', producing a structurally weak first word per block regardless of K. Raising K (safe at K>=96) likely only dilutes the weak-word proportion in the aggregate stream rather than removing the defect structurally; dilution hypothesis not yet verified further.

nodes.label: Candidate A: Widen o to 8-tap
nodes.rationale: Widening 'o' from 2 M[] taps back to the original 8-tap build_o() formula may diffuse the first word per block enough in a single mixing round because entropy input is much richer. Isolates one variable: only the 'o' line changes; update formula and ra_init_state_singleblock stay unchanged; no other ops from pruned_prng.c (ROT_A/ROT_B/SHL9 etc.) added, per explicit user request.

nodes.label: Pre-Mix Seed vs. Mixing Rounds Distinction
nodes.norm_label: pre-mix seed vs. mixing rounds distinction
nodes.rationale: General lesson from this experiment: richer/better-mixed seed entropy fed into a weak (too-few-rounds) transform does not fix the transform's statistical weakness. Fixing insufficient diffusion requires applying the transform more times (more rounds/cycles) before the first output, not a better-mixed single input -- consistent with why a full/partial warm-up cycle (rejected earlier for cost reasons) was the only approach that closed the original BCFN defect.

nodes.label: Single-Round Transform Weakness (K=1)
nodes.rationale: K=1 runs the singleblock permutation cycle exactly one iteration (always i=255, reading only M[5]/M[6]). Pre-mixing the seed (cons and M[]) before the cycle does not help because the weakness is in the transform's insufficient bit diffusion after a single application, not in the entropy quality of its inputs -- PractRand BCFN detects the predictable near-bit structure produced by one round of rot32((a>>13)^a, b), regardless of how well-mixed a/b's inputs are.
